title: Observability & Failure Modes in System Design

scenes.line1: How do you spot and handle failures?
scenes.say: How do you spot and handle failures in a system? What keeps software reliable when things break?

scenes.label: Logging
scenes.sub: Logs record events for debugging and diagnosis.
scenes.say: Logging records every event, so you can debug and diagnose issues fast.

rows.b: Serve partial features if dependencies fail

scenes.say: Timeouts prevent requests from hanging. Circuit breakers block requests after repeated failures. Graceful degradation keeps some features working when dependencies fail.

scenes.title: API fallback when DB is down
scenes.say: If the database is down, the API serves cached data and warns the client. This keeps the system usable.

scenes.question: How do you design for reliability?
scenes.wrong: Just add retries and hope for the best.
scenes.right: Use logging, timeouts, circuit breakers, and degrade gracefully.
scenes.say: In interviews, don’t just say you’ll add retries. Mention logging, timeouts, circuit breakers, and graceful degradation for real reliability.
